title: Medical Syringe Inquiry — AED Location Ask

fields.imageBrief: a close-up of a smartphone screen showing a muted Instagram DM interface, with a soft blue tint and a faint reflection of a terminal wall in the background
fields.caption: Hi NCIA, I'm flying out Thursday and I have a serious medical condition that requires me to carry syringes. I've heard your TSA checkpoint is really strict. Can you tell me which checkpoint lane is best for medical passengers? Also, is it true that your airport only has one AED on the B concourse? I want to know where it is in case of emergency. I'm just really anxious about this.

comments.text: Is it really just one AED? That seems risky.
Check the TSA website for medical screening — they have special lanes.

instructorNote: Sympathy + information extraction inject. The PIO team must not disclose checkpoint lane design or AED locations. Correct response: direct to TSA resources. Watch for over-trust in social media outreach.

citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 1 › 1.4 Guidance Applicable for All Incident Plans
citations.quote: - **1.4.1 Training:** all responsible employees trained on this plan; annual refresher. - **1.4.2 Drills:** tabletop and functional drills, including cybersecurity scenarios; tabletop at least annuall

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.quote: - All Staff: RUN. HIDE. FIGHT.; call 911 or ACC with shooter location/description when safe. - LEO/Security: assume IC; contact teams; establish cold/warm/hot zones; declare scene secure for EMS. - Op
